title: Balls, Races, Water, Ice
bigQuestion: Why do ball games, races, swimming, and ice games need different places?

story.title: Four Doors in One School
story.kicker: A class walks past a gym, a field, a pool door, and a cold rink poster.
paragraphs: Ms. Ortiz takes her class down the school hall. First they peek in the gym. The floor is wood. Two hoops hang at the ends. A red ball sits in a bin.
Next they look out at the grass. White lines make a big rectangle. "That grass is for soccer," she says. "The rectangle is called a pitch."
They pass a door with a picture of water. A sign says Pool. Another poster shows ice skates. "Water and ice need their own rooms," she says. "A field cannot hold them."
Back in class she writes four words: ball, race, water, ice. "Each kind of play has a place. Today we learn the names of those places."
story.think: Which of the four doors is most like a place near your school?

lessons.title: A Soccer Pitch
lessons.mainIdea: Association football, called soccer in the United States, is played on a grass or turf rectangle called a pitch.
reading: In 1863, clubs in London wrote shared rules for a kicking game. They formed the Football Association. People in the United States often call that game *soccer*.
The field is a *pitch*. It is a long rectangle of grass or turf. Two goals stand at the ends. The ball must stay inside the lines most of the time.

words.d: the kicking game whose rules were written in London in 1863
the rectangle of grass or turf used for soccer

look.title: The 1863 meeting
look.text: On 26 October 1863, football clubs met at the Freemasons' Tavern in London and began the Football Association, so different towns could use the same kicking rules.
look.cite: The Football Association, founding meeting, London, 26 October 1863 (standard history of association football)
look.prompt: Why did clubs from different towns need one set of rules?

check.q: When did London clubs form the Football Association?
check.why: The Football Association began in London in 1863.

check.q: What is the soccer field called?
check.why: The reading calls the rectangle a pitch.

check.q: What stands at the ends of a pitch?
check.why: Two goals stand at the ends of the pitch.

lessons.title: A Gym and a Hoop
lessons.mainIdea: Basketball began in 1891 in a gym in Springfield, Massachusetts, when James Naismith hung peach baskets.
reading: In December 1891, *James Naismith* taught in Springfield, Massachusetts. Winter kept his class inside. He needed a game that fit a gym.
He hung peach *baskets* on the balcony. Players threw a soccer ball toward the baskets. That indoor game became basketball.

words.d: the teacher who invented basketball in 1891
the peach basket, and later the hoop, that players throw toward

look.title: Naismith's winter problem
look.text: Naismith wrote that he needed an indoor game for a class at the International YMCA Training School in Springfield in December 1891. He used a soccer ball and two peach baskets.
look.cite: James Naismith, Basketball: Its Origin and Development (1941); Basketball Hall of Fame, Springfield, Massachusetts
look.prompt: Why did Naismith invent a game for a gym instead of a field?

check.q: In what year did Naismith hang the peach baskets?
check.why: The reading dates the gym game to December 1891.

check.q: What did he hang on the balcony?
check.why: He hung peach baskets for the new indoor game.

lessons.title: A Track Is 400 Meters
lessons.mainIdea: A standard outdoor running track is 400 meters around in the inside lane.
reading: A running *track* is an oval path. Runners stay in lanes. The inside lane of a standard outdoor track is 400 meters around.
World Athletics is the group that writes many track rules. School tracks in the United States often use that same 400-meter size so times can be compared.

words.d: an oval path with lanes for running races
a marked strip a runner stays in during a race

look.cite: World Athletics Technical Rules, standard outdoor running track length

check.q: How long is one lap in the inside lane outdoors?
check.why: A standard outdoor track is 400 meters around in the inside lane.

choices: a marked strip for one runner
check.why: A lane is the marked strip a runner stays in.

lessons.title: Races in Ancient Olympia
lessons.mainIdea: The ancient Olympic Games in Greece included running races in a stadium.
reading: Long ago, people ran races at *Olympia* in Greece. Those games are called the ancient Olympic Games. A main race was a sprint down a stadium.
The stadium was a long dirt path, not a modern 400-meter oval. Still, it was a place built for a race. A race needs a path people can see.

words.d: the place in Greece where the ancient Olympic Games were held

look.title: Two race paths
look.text: Look at a long straight dirt stadium in old Olympia. Then look at a modern oval track with eight painted lanes. Both are paths built so a race has a place.

check.why: The reading places those games at Olympia in Greece.

choices: a long dirt path for a race
check.why: It was a long dirt path, not a modern oval.

check.q: What does a race need, in this lesson?
check.why: A race needs a visible path.

lessons.title: A Pool Has a Measured Length
lessons.mainIdea: Many United States school pools are 25 yards long so swim times can be compared.
reading: A swimming *pool* is a tank built to hold water. The length is measured. Many school and club pools in the United States are 25 yards long.
Swimmers race from one wall to the other. A 25-yard pool is called short course yards. Longer pools of 50 meters are used in many world meets.

words.d: a tank built to hold water for swimming
a unit of length; many U.S. school pools are 25 yards long

choices: a tank built to hold water
check.why: A pool is a tank built to hold water.

check.q: How long is an Olympic-size pool?
check.why: The reading says many world meets use 50-meter pools.

lessons.title: Ice Needs a Rink
lessons.mainIdea: Ice hockey in North America is played on a rink about 200 feet long.
reading: Ice hockey needs frozen water. That place is a *rink*. In North America a National Hockey League rink is about 200 feet long and 85 feet wide.
A dry gym floor cannot hold that ice. A grass pitch cannot hold it either. Ice play needs a cold room made for ice.

words.d: the ice floor used for hockey and some skating games

choices: ice needs a cold room made for ice
check.why: Ice play needs a cold room. Grass cannot hold the ice.
